exposure: components of caesarean delivery quality (access to CS, diagnosis, procedure, postoperative care)
patient demographic and referral characteristics (age, distance from hospital, referral status, transport method)
characteristics of CS care (admission examination completeness, partograph use, CS rate, response time, emergency status, indications, type of anesthesia, anaesthetist type)
outcome: fulfillment of caesarean delivery quality criteria
cohort: 579 women who underwent caesarean section, with an average age of 26.5 years, mostly living more than 5km from the hospital and referred from other facilities, in 12 randomly selected hospitals in Benin.
finding: Caesarean section care in Benin hospitals only partially met quality criteria, with persistent difficulties in access, frequent diagnostic errors, and excessive delays contributing to the lack of quality, alongside a maternal mortality rate of 2000 per 100,000 deliveries and a perinatal mortality rate of 7.4%.
